subject.title: [Feature]: Supports Windows 11 MSYS environment and Fishshell.

question: Should OpenClaw officially support `install.sh` under Windows MSYS2/MINGW, or should Windows Unix-like shells remain outside the supported installer matrix?
rationale: The source change is technically plausible, but it changes the documented Windows support boundary and requires deciding whether `install.sh` should own native-Windows edge cases beyond WSL2.

options.title: Support MSYS2/MINGW with proof
options.body: Add explicit MSYS2/MINGW detection, Windows-safe install choices, fish PATH handling or guidance, docs, tests, and a real Windows smoke before treating the path as supported.

options.title: Document unsupported
options.body: Keep the guard and update the installer/docs to clearly route MSYS2/MINGW users to PowerShell or WSL2 instead of silently implying Unix-like Windows shells are supported.

options.title: Split fish from MSYS2
options.body: Handle fish PATH guidance for supported Unix platforms separately while leaving the Windows MSYS2/MINGW installer boundary undecided.

recommendation.title: Support MSYS2/MINGW with proof
recommendation.body: Add explicit MSYS2/MINGW detection, Windows-safe install choices, fish PATH handling or guidance, docs, tests, and a real Windows smoke before treating the path as supported.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current code-history signal for installer and Windows install behavior points to vincentkoc.
